title: Idempotent chunk IDs, backpressure signals, and reconnect behavior for SSE
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement:
We need a robust Server-Sent Events (SSE) streaming contract for the Core API that: 1) allows clients to resume partially-delivered responses without replaying already-applied chunks; 2) provides a low-overhead backpressure mechanism so clients can indicate they are temporarily overwhelmed; and 3) remains compatible with older clients that rely only on standard SSE 'id' or plain text chunks.

Current behavior and pain points:
- Some clients will reconnect mid-response and reprocess duplicated fragments, causing duplicate function/tool invocations or incorrect structured output state.
- Using only the SSE "id" header is brittle: different runtime variants and model pipelines may assign ids differently, and we can't guarantee stable semantics across rollouts.
- There's no lightweight way for clients to tell the server to slow the stream (buffering/backpressure) without tearing down the connection and losing streaming state.

Goal:
Provide server and client-compatible semantics to: 1) uniquely identify atomic token/chunk groups across reconnects, 2) allow clients to acknowledge the last-applied chunk to resume, and 3) let clients signal soft backpressure so the server can temporarily pause or reduce rate/batch size without aborting the response.

Scope for this ticket:
- Design and implement an "idempotent_chunk_id" field for SSE control events and ensure runtime emits stable chunk identifiers for a given response across short reconnect windows.
- Add a compact "X-Stream-Flow" control event that carries backpressure signals (PAUSE/RESUME/LOW_WATERMARK) with suggested hold-time and keepalive semantics.
- Implement a reconnect resume protocol that prefers explicit last-applied chunk IDs over raw byte offsets or SSE 'id' when available.
- Provide a compatibility fallback for older clients (retain SSE text/event: message bodies and standard id header behavior).
proposed_solution:
High-level approach:
1) Chunk identity: the runtime will emit a monotonically increasing UUID-lite (12 byte base62) per logical chunk group; fields: chunk_id, sequence_number (within chunk), and chunk_type (text/token/function_call/boundary). The server includes chunk_id in a compact control event (event: chunk-meta) before or alongside content chunks. Chunk IDs are stable for the lifetime of the response and for a configured resume window (default 30s after stream end).
2) Resume semantics: clients persist the last fully applied chunk_id. On reconnect clients send ?resume_from=chunk_id or include a control header Last-Applied-Chunk in an initial HTTP GET. The server will replay only chunks after that id. If chunk_id is unknown (expired or evicted), server falls back to conservative resume: restart from beginning or return a resume failure control event instructing client to re-request non-stream endpoint.
3) Backpressure control: introduce event: stream-flow with payloads {action:PAUSE|RESUME|LOW_WATERMARK, suggested_ms}. Clients emit these as a small POST to /stream-control or via a single SSE client->server TODO event (if using bidirectional WebSocket in private deployments). For hosted SSE (unidirectional), we will support a short HTTP POST control path (authenticated using connection token) so clients can ask server to slow token emission. Server responds with acknowledgement and applies a temporary rate reduce/batching change for that connection.
4) Compatibility layer: if client does not request resume or send Last-Applied-Chunk, server will continue to supply plain SSE id and data events exactly as before. The new control events are additive and optional.

Implementation notes:
- Runtime: add chunk-id assignment in the tokenization/streaming stage (downstream of kernel scheduling) to ensure chunk boundaries align with function-call boundaries and structured JSON emissions.
- Storage: keep a transient per-response resume window in runtime memory (configurable TTL); avoid durable storage to keep costs down.
- API: document new query param resume_from and Last-Applied-Chunk header, and the stream-flow control POST (schema provided in docs).
- Observability: add per-request metrics: resume_attempts, resume_success_rate, duplicate_chunks_sent, and flow_control_events_received.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Adding chunk IDs increases payload metadata slightly; we chose compact base62 IDs to limit overhead (~12 bytes).
- Relying on in-memory resume windows avoids heavy storage but risks resume failures when runtime evicts entries or on cross-node reconnections. To mitigate we will extend the resume window for enterprise Dedicated customers and expose a configuration knob.
- Backpressure via an HTTP control POST opens a new surface to authenticate and rate-limit; requires careful auth token handling to avoid abuse.
- Some older SDKs will ignore the new control events; compatibility mode keeps existing guarantees but prevents resume benefits for those clients.
- Implementing stable chunk ids ties into how kernels batch token generation; small changes in bundling could change chunk boundaries. We will pin chunk semantics to logical output boundaries (function call complete, structured JSON object close, newline boundary for plain text) to minimize churn.

Milestones:

- Runtime implementation (chunk-id assignment + transient resume store) — PR targeted by 2026-03-12
- Control POST endpoint and auth integration — PR targeted by 2026-03-14
- SDK updates (python/js) to persist last-applied chunk and auto-resume — merge by 2026-03-18
- E2E tests + chaos tests (disconnects at random offsets) — 2026-03-19 to 2026-03-21

Implementation tasks (engineering owners):
- Liam O'Connor: runtime chunk assignment, resume window store, metrics (ENG-12134-A)
- Priya Nair: control endpoint, auth integration, rate-limits (ENG-12134-B)
- SDK team: auto-resume + backpressure control helper methods (ENG-12134-C)

acceptance_criteria:
1) Server emits chunk-meta events with chunk_id for every logical chunk; unit tests verifying stable chunk_id for identical response across minor runtime restarts (within resume window).
2) Client can reconnect with Last-Applied-Chunk header and receive only subsequent chunks (integration test with deterministic input).
3) Backpressure control POST reduces token emission rate by at least 50% for the specified suggested_ms in 95th percentile of cases.
4) Default compatibility behavior unchanged: existing clients that ignore new events see same stream format and no regressions.
5) Metrics available in Console: resume_attempts, resume_success_rate, duplicate_chunks_sent per-model per-region.
6) SDKs provide helper to persist last-applied chunk and optionally auto-retry resume; ship python and js within this cycle.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for chunk-id generation determinism and uniqueness.
- Integration test harness simulating reconnect mid-chunk, reconnect after last-applied chunk, and resume failure when chunk expired.
- Load test to measure overhead: measure latency and additional bytes per token across 10k concurrent streaming responses. Overhead goal: <2% token throughput regression.
- Chaos test: random TCP kill/reconnect at different places in response; assert no duplicated function invocation for structured outputs.
- Security test: abuse scenarios for POST /stream-control (replay, forged token, rate-limit exhaustion).
rollout_plan:
- Feature behind runtime flag and API version toggle.
- Canary 10% traffic for internal customers and CI jobs for 48 hours; monitor duplicate_chunks_sent, resume_success_rate, and error_budget.
- If regressions detected: automatic rollback to previous behavior (flag off) and open postmortem.
- After 1 week of stable canary, expand to all hosted traffic and ship SDK minor release notes.
- Dedicated/private customers can opt into extended resume windows via configuration (support ticket flow).
dependencies_and_blockers:
- Dependency: ENG-11021 (SSE fragmentation/resume protocol groundwork) for baseline framing guarantees.
- Blocking: final auth model for control POST needs completion from security team (pending PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/4197).
- SDK teams must land helper prior to full rollout; otherwise clients will not benefit from resume semantics.

Create Console dash: 'Streaming Resume & Flow' with per-model and per-region split. Link: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/streaming-resume
notes:
- We intentionally choose compact base62 chunk IDs over full UUIDs to limit bandwidth for high-throughput streams.
- If clients prefer a conservative approach, SDK helper will expose an option to always re-request non-streaming endpoint upon any reconnect.
- Consider adding optional cryptographic HMAC of chunk payload for high-trust resumed delivery (future work).
